text:
maria: FYI Trailhead (dedicated pool 'tdesk-prod') reporting sustained 429s + high token latency since 09:12 UTC. Customer says responses include 'burst credits exhausted' header. Sample curl & headers below.

jordan: pinged them — they ran a marketing push at 09:10 and saw a sudden sustained spike. Not a one-off test. Avg seq length ~600 tokens.

ashu: assigning to eng-infra to triage. Can you paste autoscaler events + admission logs? My immediate hunch: burst credit exhaustion + scale-up lag. pool id?

maria: pool_id: pool-907 (us-west2). Autoscaler shows scale-up requested at 09:13 but new nodes/pods became Ready at 09:19. Admission log snippet: 

```
2026-03-16T09:12:49Z admission-controller pool=pool-907 action=reject reason=headroom_low burst_credits=0 tokens_requested=4800
2026-03-16T09:12:50Z admission-controller pool=pool-907 action=reject reason=headroom_low burst_credits=0 tokens_requested=5200
2026-03-16T09:13:01Z autoscaler pool=pool-907 event=scale_up requested=2_gpus
2026-03-16T09:19:24Z autoscaler pool=pool-907 event=scale_complete added=2_gpus
```

Also sample response header from customer: `X-Redwood-Burst-Credits: 0`, `X-Redwood-Admission: throttled`, HTTP 429 body.

linh: thanks. Do we have per-tenant qps breakdown during the spike? Also check node-level GPU mem pressure — that can delay placement even if autoscaler requested capacity.

ashu: ran quick query against metrics (09:08–09:20): tenant `bluebird` consumed ~65% of pool tokens/sec for a 3m window starting 09:10. Node-5 GPU memory usage peaked 98% at 09:12 and OOM-kill=false but placement backpressure observed. Not a classic "noisy neighbor" attack but highly skewed load.

maria: customer also reported seeing billing webhook retries earlier in the morning — they worry credits went negative. @billing-bot any correlating billing events?

billing-bot: Billing system logs: billing webhook delivery delayed (retry loop) between 09:06–09:20 for account trailhead-230. Payment succeeded at 09:20 and credits reconciled at 09:20:35. No manual block, but auto-credit top-up happened after the spike.

linh: that aligns: admission controller enforces burst credits+headroom until top-up; if credits are 0 and headroom insufficient we reject until autoscale + credit top-up complete. Short-term mitigation options: emergency allowlist or temporary headroom bump on pool. Longer term: prewarm policy for known promos, faster pod prewarm, per-tenant soft caps.

ashu: applied emergency override: adhoc_headroom=+2 GPUs (equivalent) to pool-907 at 09:24. Customer reported successful calls ~09:25 and latencies normalized.

maria: customer confirms calls recovered and 429s stopped. They asked for a short write-up on repro steps so they can test before future campaigns. Below are the repro steps we used and the tech artifacts to collect.

Repro steps (for eng/playbook):
1) Run load generator to emulate their traffic pattern: sustained 450–550 RPS, mean seq length 600 tokens for 3–5 minutes.

Sample loadgen (k6 + inline script):
```
# rough example
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 3m --out json=out.json loadtest.js
// loadtest.js should send POST /v1/generate with avg prompt producing ~600 tokens
```

2) Delay billing webhook (simulate 10–15m webhook retry) so account credit top-up happens after initial spike.
3) Simulate node prewarm/placement delay: cordon + drain a single node to reproduce placement latency, or add artificial GPU mem pressure on node to hit 90%+.

Collect: admission-controller logs, autoscaler events, `kubectl get pods -w` timeline, node GPU metrics, per-tenant tokens/sec time series, and the `X-Redwood-Burst-Credits` header traces.

ashu: adding small engineering note — admission decisions include both credits and headroom. If credits==0 but headroom exists we still allow some requests until headroom threshold; in this incident headroom was consumed by `bluebird` spike while autoscaler was provisioning new GPUs that took ~6 minutes to become ready. We should consider: faster prewarm image pull, optimistic placement, or an admission grace window for recently-requested scale-ups.

jordan: customer happy for now. I'll open a follow-up ticket for PM/infra to discuss prewarm + headroom policy and ask about a one-time SLO credit. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks team — I'll attach logs and the collected traces to the ticket. Closing thread once postmortem doc created. :party_parrot:
